paper.title: Learning to Bid in FCR Markets: A Best-of-Both-Worlds Approach

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated uniform-price auction (FCR) with stochastic opposing bids
unmapped: Learner observes only market-level bandit feedback (clearing price and allocation), from which semi-bandit feedback on active coordinates of the combinatorial representation H subset {0,1}^N is reconstructed
Opposing bid vectors beta^t drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution D; utility is a linear function h(b)^T W(beta) of the bid encoding, bounded by the number of units K
Multi-unit uniform-price auction with K = D_max,s units and discretized bid grid; marginal costs known to the bidder
settings.definition_quote: The opposing bids are stochastic. This setting is defined by $\mathcal{D}$, a distribution from which, for each timestep $t \in [T]$, the opposing bids $\betavec^t$ are sampled.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated uniform-price auction (FCR) with adversarial opposing bids
unmapped: Learner observes only market-level bandit feedback (clearing price and allocation), from which semi-bandit feedback on active coordinates is reconstructed
Opposing bids form any fixed sequence; utility linear h(b)^T W(beta^t), bounded in terms of K
settings.definition_quote: The opposing bids are adversarial. In this case, the opposing bids $(\betavec^t)_{t \in [T]}$ can be any fixed sequence.

algorithms.name: BOB Algorithm for Semi-Bandit (FTRL with hybrid Tsallis/log regularizer, Zimmert et al. 2019)

conditions: Assumptions 1-2: provider participates in a single country; clearing price < 1

source.quote: The pseudo regret incurred by \autoref{algo : bob_bidder} is upper bounded, in the stochastic opposing bid case, by \tilde{R}_T = \mathcal{O} ( \log T ) and in the adversarial opposing bid case by R_T = \mathcal{O} ( \sqrt{T} ) where $\mathcal{O}$ hides problem-dependent constants.

results.notes: Stated as a simplified restatement of Theorem 2 of Zimmert et al. (2019) applied to the auction reduction; O hides problem-dependent constants (gaps, N, K). Possibly requires unique optimal action as in Zimmert et al., not stated here.

conditions: Assumptions 1-2: provider participates in a single country; clearing price < 1

source.quote: The pseudo regret incurred by \autoref{algo : bob_bidder} is upper bounded, in the stochastic opposing bid case, by \tilde{R}_T = \mathcal{O} ( \log T ) and in the adversarial opposing bid case by R_T = \mathcal{O} ( \sqrt{T} ) where $\mathcal{O}$ hides problem-dependent constants.

results.notes: R_T defined with sup over fixed bids outside the expectation, i.e. pseudo-regret. O hides problem-dependent constants (dimension N, K). Adapted from Zimmert et al. (2019).
